title: Minestrone
subtitle: Italian vegetable and pasta soup
excerpt: A thick, vegetable-loaded Italian soup with cannellini beans, seasonal vegetables, pasta, and a generous finish of Parmesan and basil pesto. A meal in a bowl.

recipe.sourceNotes: Minestrone (literally 'big soup') is Italy's most versatile and least fixed recipe. It is a soup of seasonal vegetables, beans, and pasta or rice, that varies by region and by what is available. Northern Italian versions include rice; Southern versions include pasta; Roman versions include guanciale and pork rind. There is no single authoritative recipe because it has always been a way of using what is in the vegetable garden. What is consistent is the soffritto base (onion, celery, carrot cooked slowly in olive oil), the inclusion of beans for protein, and the finishing with a drizzle of good olive oil and grated cheese. A spoonful of basil pesto added at the end is a Genovese tradition that lifts the entire soup.

content.text: The soffritto must be cooked slowly until the onion and celery are completely soft and sweet: at least 12 minutes over medium-low heat. This is the flavour base of the entire soup. Add the pasta in the last 10 minutes of cooking so it does not become overcooked and mushy. Minestrone thickens significantly on standing as the pasta absorbs liquid; add more stock or water when reheating.

items.preparation: small shapes: macaroni, ditalini, or broken spaghetti

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Fry the onion, celery, and carrot for 12 minutes until soft and sweet. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the courgette, tinned tomatoes, stock, bay, and thyme. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes. Add the cannellini beans and green beans.

Add the pasta and cook for the time stated on the packet. In the last 3 minutes, stir in the kale. Remove the bay and thyme. Taste for seasoning. Ladle into bowls. Drizzle with olive oil and scatter with Parmesan.
